newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FOCUS - DSM profits rise, sees growth.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - DSM profits rise, sees growth.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM NV on Wednesday reported 1997 first-half net profit up 13 percent at 465 million guilders and predicted "clearly higher" earnings for the full year.
Higher sales volumes and profit margins drove a sharp rise in earnings from DSM's polymers and hydrocarbons division.
But operating profits from industrial and fine chemicals were depressed by maintenance shutdowns and plant revamping.

DSM said it expected earnings for the whole of 1997 to be clearly higher than in 1996. "As far as can be judged at present, in the next few months current market conditions, which are good, will not change significantly," it said in a statement.
"Assuming that the macro-economic situation will remain stable, we expect our results for the whole of 1997 to be clearly higher than those for 1996."

Despite the upbeat forecast, DSM shares slipped in Amsterdam after the results, which were at the lower end of the range of analysts' estimates. By 1565 GMT the shares had shed 11.50 guilders, or 5.00 percent, to 218.50 guilders.
"I thought the results were a little disappointing, especially the developments in industrial and fine chemicals," Nils van Elzelingen, analyst at NIB Securities said.

"The forecast for the second half year was quite new and they might just exceed our estimates for the full year. But in general we think the outlook for DSM in the next two years is not so good and our recommendation remains at Underperformer."
In the industrial chemicals division, higher selling prices for caprolactam, melamine and acrylonitrile, due in part to the higher dollar, boosted year-on-year sales figures.
But DSM said operating results for caprolactam and melamine were lower because of maintenance shutdowns and production outages.
Fertilisers booked sharply lower operating results because of lower selling prices and an overhaul of one of the group's ammonia plants.
Fine chemicals showed a "considerable increase" in both sales and operating profits, due mainly to acquisitions, higher selling prices and the strong dollar, DSM said.

Net sales for industrial and fine chemicals as a whole were up at 2.08 billion guilders versus 1.90 billion in first half 1996, but operating results were down sharply at 183 million guilders from a year-earlier 314 million.

The drop was compensated for by a strong rise in profits at the polymers and performance materials division, whose sales rose to 2.82 billion guilders in first half 1997 from 2.06 billion in the same period of 1996, while operating profits jumped to 264 million from 72 million.
DSM said the rise in sales was caused by higher sales volumes for all products and higher price levels compared with the first half of 1996.
Higher sales volumes for hydrocarbons, polyethylene and polypropylene were the main reason for the higher operating profit in the first half.

"Although higher margins were achieved on hydrocarbons and polyethylene, margins on polypropylene, elastomers and engineering plastics were lower due to increased raw-material costs," the company said.
But analysts said the boost from polymers might be short lived.

"Turnover rose nicely in the various divisions, notably in hydrocarbons/polymers. This underlines the healthy economic growth in Europe, and consequent growth in demand," said analyst Ab Barneveldt of Generale Bank.

"Prospects for 1997 seem good, but additional capacity will lead to overcapacity in hydrocarbons and polymers from the fourth quarter and it will be felt in the margins in 1998. We maintain our Hold rating for DSM."

In the company's smaller divisions, operating profits for resins and plastics grew to 88 million guilders from 74 million in the first half of 1996. Operating profits from energy and other activities fell to 107 million guilders from a year-earlier 122 million.
